findings.title: remove_member bypasses GroupUser callbacks and the user_count counter cache
findings.body: `group.users.delete(user_id)` deletes the join rows of a `has_many :through` association, whose default deletion strategy is `delete_all` (raw SQL on `group_users`). This skips all `GroupUser` callbacks and the `counter_cache: "user_count"` on `GroupUser#group`, so `groups.user_count` is never decremented and side effects previously performed by `Group#remove` (title / trust-level / primary-group housekeeping) are not run. The result is a permanently wrong member count shown in the admin UI and in the new `members` endpoint's `meta.total`, plus stale user titles. Use `group.remove(user)` with a looked-up `User` record instead. Additionally, `CollectionProxy#delete` with an integer id performs a `find`, so a stale/bogus `user_id` raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` (500) instead of a clean error.

findings.title: create silently drops alias_level
findings.body: `create` only assigns `name` and `visible`, but the client's `Group#asJSON` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js) always posts `alias_level` as well. An admin who picks an alias level while creating a new group has that choice silently discarded; the group is created with the default alias level and the admin must save a second time to apply it. Assign `group.alias_level` in `create` the same way `update` does.

findings.title: update forces visible=false whenever the param is absent
findings.body: `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` is executed unconditionally, so any PUT to `/admin/groups/:id` that does not include `visible` (or sends a JSON boolean `true` rather than the string "true") will set the group to invisible. Since `update` is now the only way to change group attributes, a partial update from any other client silently hides the group. Only assign when the param is present, and accept boolean values.

findings.title: add_members crashes when usernames is sent as an array
findings.body: `usernames.split(",")` assumes a String. If a client posts `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b` (a perfectly natural encoding, and the shape the old API accepted via `Array(actions[:add])`), `params.require(:usernames)` returns an Array and `split` raises `NoMethodError`, producing a 500. Normalize with `Array.wrap(...)`/`to_s.split(",")` before iterating.

findings.title: members endpoint accepts unbounded and negative limit/offset
findings.body: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are passed straight to the query. Any anonymous visitor can request `?limit=1000000` on a large group and force the server to load and serialize the whole membership (cheap DoS vector), and `?limit=-1` or `?offset=-1` makes PostgreSQL raise "LIMIT must not be negative" / "OFFSET must not be negative", returning a 500. Clamp both values (e.g. limit between 1 and 100, offset >= 0).

findings.title: GET /groups/:name/members response shape changed with no spec coverage
findings.body: The endpoint previously returned a bare JSON array of serialized users; it now returns `{members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}`. This is a breaking change for any external consumer or plugin hitting the public members endpoint, and no spec was added or updated for the new shape or for the pagination behaviour (spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb is untouched in this PR, so any existing assertion on the array response is now wrong). Add/update specs covering the new payload, the default limit, and the offset handling.

findings.title: totalPages off-by-one creates a phantom empty last page
findings.body: `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` over-counts whenever `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`: with 50 members and limit 50 it reports 2 pages, and `next` is enabled (showingLast compares currentPage to totalPages), so the admin can page to an empty member list showing "2/2". Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`. The same off-by-one is reinforced in Group#findMembers, which clamps offset to `user_count` instead of `user_count - 1`, allowing an offset that returns zero rows.

findings.title: Public group members page is now silently truncated to 50 users
findings.body: `GroupsController#members` now applies a default limit of 50 to every group (previously only automatic groups were paginated), but this template has no pagination controls and the group-members route just calls `model.findMembers()` once. For any group with more than 50 members the public page now shows only the first 50 with no indication that members are missing and no way to load the rest. Either add pagination/infinite scroll here or request the full list for this view.

findings.title: remove_member spec uses the wrong HTTP verb and only covers the automatic-group guard
findings.body: `xhr :put, :remove_member` is used while the route is registered as `delete "members"` (config/routes.rb), so the test exercises a verb that does not exist in production routing. More importantly, the only non-automatic test removes an existing member and asserts `group.users.count == 0`; there is no coverage for `group.user_count` staying consistent, nor for a `user_id` that is not a member / does not exist (which currently raises RecordNotFound). Fix the verb and add those cases.

findings.title: findMembers returns undefined for unnamed groups, breaking promise-based callers
findings.body: When `name` is empty `findMembers` now returns `undefined` instead of the previous `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])`. Callers treat the return value as a promise (`actions.next`/`previous` return it, and `removeMember`/`addMembers` chain off `findMembers`), so for a new, unsaved group any code that calls `.then()` on the result will throw. Return a resolved promise instead.
